summary: Agent quickstart: tool call arguments fail schema validation / JSON parse error (TypeScript template)
description:
Issue summary
- Customer running the RAG+agent TypeScript quickstart reports repeated failures when the agent attempts to call tools.
- Failure presents as a tool schema validation error and the agent loop aborts instead of recovering.

Impact
- Agent template is effectively unusable for some prompts; user sees 500 from local app route /chat and no final answer.
- Blocks evaluation and onboarding for quickstarts.

Customer report
- "Agent keeps crashing on tool call. Looks like tool args aren’t valid JSON or don’t match schema. We expected the template to be resilient to this and to retry / ask the model to reformat." (DevFoundry)

Environment
- Template: redwood-quickstarts TypeScript RAG+agent template (internal beta branch per README)
- Runtime: Node 20.x, macOS
- Redwood API: Hosted (prod), region us-east
- Observability: local OTel collector disabled (not required to reproduce)

Steps to reproduce (Support validated)
1) Scaffold TS template (rag-agent) and set REDWOOD_API_KEY.
2) Start server: npm run dev
3) Use the default chat UI or curl /chat with the following user prompt:
   "Search the docs for 'streaming reconnect', summarize the recommended approach, and cite the relevant section."
4) Agent attempts to call tool: search_docs(query: string, limit?: number)
5) Failure occurs during tool arguments parsing/validation.

Expected behavior
- If tool args are invalid JSON OR fail schema validation, the agent should:
  a) log a structured tool error with safe redaction
  b) ask the model to re-emit the tool call arguments strictly matching the JSON schema (or fall back to a safe default)
  c) continue the agent loop up to max iterations

Actual behavior
- Template throws during JSON.parse / zod validation and aborts the request.

Observed error (redacted)
- Error class: ToolSchemaValidationError (template)
- Message (example):
  "tool_call.arguments is not valid JSON" OR "Invalid tool arguments for search_docs: expected object, received string"

Representative log snippet (customer + reproduced)
- 2025-03-07T19:12:43.118Z level=error event=tool_args_parse_failed tool_name=search_docs request_id=rwreq_01H... err="Unexpected token ' in JSON at position 1" raw_arguments="{'query':'streaming reconnect','limit':5}"
- 2025-03-07T19:12:43.119Z level=error event=agent_loop_failed request_id=rwreq_01H... err="Tool schema parse failed" iteration=1

Notes
- This appears model-dependent and prompt-dependent. Some responses emit single quotes or trailing commas in tool args; current template uses strict JSON.parse and hard-fails.
- Customer asked whether Redwood supports "lenient JSON" or a built-in repair strategy; we should implement recovery in template rather than relying on model perfection.

Request
- Fix template to handle invalid tool args robustly (repair/retry path) and improve error message for end users.
- Add troubleshooting note to docs (common error: tool schema parse) with suggested mitigations.
comments: 2025-03-07 (Priya Shah, Support) — Triage: Reproduced locally using TS rag-agent template. Tool call arguments occasionally come back as a string containing invalid JSON (single quotes). Current code path does JSON.parse(arguments) and immediately validates via zod; exception bubbles to handler and returns 500. Setting prompt temperature low reduces frequency but doesn’t eliminate.

2025-03-07 (Owen Phillips, Support) — Asked customer for exact prompt + raw tool args. Suggested immediate workaround: re-run with a system instruction: "When calling tools, output arguments as strict JSON using double quotes". Customer confirmed it helps but still sees occasional malformed args with long prompts.

2025-03-08 (Dana Lo, Eng) — Confirmed known failure mode. We need a guardrail loop: on parse/validation failure, send a corrective message back to the model ("Your tool arguments were invalid; re-emit ONLY valid JSON for the tool schema") and retry tool selection up to N times. Also cap raw tool args size in logs and redact content. I’ll patch template utilities + add tests.

2025-03-08 (Allison Grant, Observability) — Please ensure errors increment the standard metric (tool_errors_total) with reason="schema_validation" or reason="json_parse" and avoid tagging with tool arguments (cardinality + PII). Include request_id + tool_name only.

2025-03-09 (Sahana Iyer, CI) — Added a flaky repro to smoke tests: intentionally feed malformed tool args and assert the agent recovers and returns a user-facing error only after max repair attempts. We should avoid relying on actual model behavior in CI; use a mocked tool-call payload.

2025-03-10 (Dana Lo, Eng) — Fix PR opened in redwood-quickstarts (see related PR). Changes:
  - toolArgsParse(): tries JSON.parse, on failure attempts a minimal repair (replace single quotes with double quotes only when safe) and re-parse
  - if still failing, triggers "tool args repair" step (model asked to re-emit args) with max 2 attempts
  - zod validation failure follows same repair path
  - structured logs: event=tool_args_parse_failed / tool_args_validation_failed; includes request_id, tool_name, iteration, attempt
  - metrics: tool_errors_total{reason}
  - user message: "Tool call failed due to invalid arguments; retrying" (only in debug mode)
  - docs: troubleshooting section to be updated separately

2025-03-11 (Owen Phillips, Support) — Deployed fix to template main branch (customer can re-scaffold or cherry-pick). Customer confirmed the same prompt now succeeds; when malformed args occur, the agent retries and completes. Closing as resolved; leaving docs follow-up to Wei/Elliot.
resolution: Resolved by updating the TypeScript RAG+agent quickstart template to recover from tool argument JSON parse / schema validation failures. Template now retries via a repair loop (ask model to re-emit strict JSON), emits standard tool error metrics/logs, and avoids aborting the request on first failure. Customer confirmed successful run after updating to the patched template version.
